title: Reddit's new recipe for ad growth: search, shopping, and AI agents
excerpt: Reddit is countering unpredictable search traffic with a plan to beef up its advertising machine.
content_html:
By Lara O'Reilly

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

Author of the CMO Insider newsletter

2026-11-25T13:00:01.378Z

Reddit has a new ads agenda: search, shopping, and AI agents.

In an interview with CMO Insider, Reddit Chief Operating Officer Jen Wong outlined how the company is laying the groundwork to turn its highly engaged community conversations into a more automated commerce and performance ads business.

Wong said that next year, Reddit wants to start testing a model context protocol (MCP) server and agent-to-agent ad buying capabilities within its Reddit Max automated buying platform as it follows the industry into agentic ad buying. (MCP servers let AI agents securely connect to a company's data and tools.)

This month, Reddit began testing ads on its search results pages in the US. Rather than selling search ads as a separate, keyword-bidding buy in the mold of Google, Reddit is auto-placing search ads when they're relevant to the queries users are typing.

Shopping is also central to Reddit's 2027 ad road map.

This month, it launched a feature called Reddit Reviews that uses AI to compile subreddit discussions into dedicated product review pages. While there are no ads there yet, Wong advised marketers to continually upload fresh product catalogs to Reddit so reviews can be a "fulsome experience" and feed Reddit's broader product knowledge graph. It builds on the launch of Reddit Insights in 2025, which lets marketers get the pulse on sentiment and conversations around brands or topics.

The push to beef up its ad offering comes as Reddit seeks to reduce its reliance on unpredictable search traffic. Reddit is shifting to become primarily a logged-in platform, which it has said will lead to richer ad-targeting signals. The larger ads ambition is to make Reddit a more measurable performance media buy and a repeatable item in marketers' campaign budgets.

While many marketers are spinning up their own subreddits and responding to conversations about their brands across the platform, Wong drew a distinction between brands participating organically in Reddit communities and buying ads. She compared the former to search engine optimization and the latter to search engine marketing.

"If you want to drive day-to-day business growth with a reliable, repeatable outcome at scale, you market," Wong said.

Reddit is rethinking its own marketing

Reddit's ad business is growing healthily. Ad revenue increased 54% year over year to $847 million in its third quarter. The company credited demand for performance-ad products, including shopping and app-install campaigns, which each grew over 95% year over year. Wong said on the October earnings call that over 60% of the ad business is now "performance oriented."

Wall Street analysts, however, have been concerned about a slowdown in user growth. Last quarter, Reddit's daily active user count in the US fell 2% year over year, and the company warned that its global count could drop by a low double-digit percentage in the current quarter if search traffic continued to decline at the same pace. Reddit reported 130 million global daily active users in its third quarter.

Wong said marketing would play a key role in revitalizing Reddit's user growth, adding that Reddit only began investing in marketing in a concentrated way over the past 12 to 18 months.

"For the first decade, we were all word of mouth, then for the last decade we had word of mouth plus search," Wong said, adding that Reddit hadn't previously put substantial effort into converting those visitors to logged-in users.

In the third quarter, Reddit shifted its US media mix more toward app-install ads and brand marketing. The overall budget as a share of revenue remained consistent in the mid-single digits. In August, it turned subreddits into an IRL pop-up activation at a bodega in New York City, encouraging visitors to "find your corner of the internet" and pick up free swag.

Wong said the challenge of marketing Reddit is demonstrating both its vast range of topics and its intimate, personalized experience, built around individuals' assorted hobbies and tastes, from EDM to skiing and cooking.

"Conveying that is hard," Wong said. "The through line is the community."

She added that "all things are on the table" when it comes to testing new brand marketing approaches.

"We are open to trying a lot," Wong said. "The canvas is very wide because we've done nothing."

Reddit is still a long way behind the multibillion-dollar ad revenue machines of Meta, Amazon, or Google. Some brands have been hesitant about the benefit of Reddit as an advertising channel, said Jack Johnston, a VP at the performance marketing agency Tinuiti. He added that he is "very excited" about the direction the platform is headed.

"Reddit is already increasingly becoming a performance channel in its own right, but it is often underutilized and underappreciated," Johnston said. "Making shopping more seamless will not only benefit in-market Reddit users, but will also make conversion opportunities more economical for brands."
